content: The recommendations will undergo periodic review alongside other guidelines to determine their prioritization by the Executive Guideline Steering Group (GSG). If new evidence emerges that could significantly alter the current evidence base, the recommendations may be updated accordingly. Once updated recommendations are published and disseminated, any concerns regarding their validity will be promptly communicated to the guideline implementers. This communication will include details about plans for further updates to ensure the recommendations remain accurate and relevant. The World Health Organization (WHO) actively encourages suggestions for additional questions or topics to be considered in future updates of the recommendations. This process ensures that the guidelines remain comprehensive and reflective of the latest evidence and clinical needs. The references cited include a wide range of studies and resources that provide evidence and context for the recommendations. These include systematic reviews, meta-analyses, randomized controlled trials, and cost-effectiveness analyses related to maternal and perinatal health, induction of labor, and antenatal care. The references also highlight the importance of integrating human rights-based approaches and addressing inequalities in reproductive, maternal, newborn, and child health. The guideline development process involved contributions from a diverse group of experts, including obstetricians, gynecologists, midwives, public health professionals, and researchers from various countries and institutions. These experts provided input on the evidence synthesis, guideline formulation, and external review to ensure the recommendations are robust, evidence-based, and globally applicable. Critical maternal outcomes identified in the recommendations include failure to achieve vaginal delivery within 24 hours, cesarean section, uterine hyperstimulation with fetal heart rate changes, postpartum hemorrhage, uterine rupture, and severe maternal morbidity or mortality. Important maternal outcomes include unfavorable cervical changes after 24 hours, oxytocin augmentation, epidural use, uterine hyperstimulation without fetal heart rate changes, instrumental vaginal birth, meconium-stained amniotic fluid, maternal side effects (e.g., nausea, vomiting, diarrhea), maternal well-being, and dissatisfaction with care. The WHO emphasizes the importance of skilled health personnel during childbirth and the need for high-quality maternal and newborn care in health facilities. The guidelines aim to improve outcomes for mothers and newborns by providing evidence-based recommendations that address clinical decision-making, resource utilization, and patient satisfaction.
